Typed refactor: give `gone` a concrete type (e.g. `gone: GoneFacts` / `*const GoneFacts`), add `defer names.deinit(cx.a)`, and pass the held answer and the fact text as distinct named arguments.

- `zig/src/metal/sync.zig` — defines `SharedEvent` (`value`, `set`, `wait`, `deinit`) and `Event` (`deinit`). Risk: `self: SharedEvent` is passed by value, so copies share the same `id`; calling `deinit` on a copy releases the id while the original still holds it (double-release/use-after-release). Also `wait` reads an ObjC `BOOL` via `objc.msg(bool, ...)`, which is fragile if the ABI returns a wider integer. Typed refactor: make `deinit` take `*SharedEvent`, set `id` to a sentinel/undefined after release, and keep `SharedEvent` non-copyable (or wrap it in an owned handle); use a dedicated `BOOL`/`c_int` ABI for `wait`.

- `zig/src/families/hy4_flash/index_cuda.zig` — defines `Weights`, `Indexer` (`load`, `deinit`, `cacheKeys`, `poolGroups`, `select`), and `closedBy`. Risk: `pub const nope = width - 2 * rotary.pairs;` underflows (usize) if `2 * rotary.pairs > width`, silently producing a huge offset used in `rope_base = arena + (@as(u64, first_group) * width + nope) * 2` and `b.query + nope * 2`. Typed refactor: make `nope` a comptime-checked value, e.g. `pub const nope = std.math.sub(usize, width, 2 * rotary.pairs) catch @compileError("rotary pairs exceed width");`, and keep `Args.add` heterogeneous-typed via a small typed builder rather than one `inline for` over mixed `u64`/`u32`/`f32`.

- `zig/src/families/hy4_flash/moe_exl3_cuda.zig` — defines `Route`, `Routed` (`init`, `forward`, `run`), and `projection`. Risk: `init` does `defer a.free(projections)` and `defer a.free(space)` after `upload.layer(...)` / `owner.dev(space)`; if either retains host slices (`gate`/`up`/`down`, or `space`), the layer/scratch dangle. `Routed` also has no `deinit`, so `layer`/`scratch` are never released. Typed refactor: make `upload.layer` copy projections into device-owned storage (or return an owning `Layer`), and add `pub fn deinit(self: *Routed, owner: *upload.Uploader) void` that frees `scratch` and the layer.

- `zig/src/families/qwen3_5/cuda_dspine_weights.zig` — defines `Bridge` (`alloc`, `deinit`), `total`, and the start of `version`. Central claim: the native engine can run these checkpoints as stored—keeping the checkpoint’s own precision and semantics—with measured exactness and speed, while being explicit about what is not yet qualified or served.

Evidence offered:
- Nemotron 3.5 Super VL (CUDA/GB10): reads NVFP4/FP8/bf16 tensors as stored; TP=1 vs TP=2 give identical tokens (17/17 replies); `checkpoint` vs `full`: KL 0.0036–0.0137 nats, same top token 98.4%, NLL 0.0692→0.0749; cold 8,192-token prompt 4.41 s vs 7.96 s (1.81x) with similar decode; MTP drafts equal `"draft": false`; 2/4 concurrent streams equal solo runs; three-turn chats equal a cache-off server; two GB10s 46.8 tok/s vs one 38.2 tok/s; four concurrent streams 6.2 s vs 11.8 s; four-image request first token 11.45 s, draft equal, 74.4 GiB device memory.
- DeepSeek-V4.1 (CUDA, experimental): CPU generators validate geometry and record SHA256 provenance; `aot-needs` runs the family’s symbolic planner on CPU and never opens a CUDA driver; external Triton reference tools compile for the actual target SM; install ARM64 binaries with real runtime/family CUDA images; compile-only targets use inert synthetic images and cannot produce a serving qualification receipt.
- MiniMax H3 (Metal/M5): bf16 weights read in place, bf16 activations, fp32 sums; a test tool beside the engine; 13 kernels registered against their formulas; prints first-forward velocities against the reference velocities the case holds; `dense` is kernel-work only, not the trained configuration.

Weakest inference: the jump from “the native engine runs these checkpoints with measured exactness/speed” to “they are ready to serve” is weakest for DeepSeek-V4.1 (and, to a lesser degree, MiniMax H3). DeepSeek is explicitly experimental; CPU build/host-test results do not qualify a checkpoint or GPU, and compile-only targets cannot produce a serving qualification receipt—so the evidence supports asset generation and binary builds, not serving readiness. MiniMax H3 is a test tool, not the lane core/server, and its `dense` mode is not the trained configuration, so kernel-contract registration alone does not prove the trained denoising forward matches the reference.

What would settle it: for DeepSeek-V4.1, run the actual serving path on the target GPU with the real checkpoint and compare outputs against the official/reference implementation, producing a serving qualification receipt (not compile-only). For MiniMax H3, run the full routed (not `dense`) denoising forward on the M5 tensor units and compare final video/audio rows and first-forward velocities against the reference case, confirming the top-20% video-tile selection and pooled branch.
